title: Positive powers of line bundles on normal schemes admit connected affine group linearizations
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] such that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $a:G\times_k X\to X$ be any action, satisfying identity and associativity as morphism equalities [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $L$ be any invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Then there is an integer $m\geq1$ such that $L^{\otimes m}$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] admits a $G$-linearization. A $G$-linearization of an invertible module $M$ means an isomorphism $\theta:p_2^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*M$ on $G\times_k X$ of pulled-back modules [def-pc-module-pullback], whose restriction along the identity is $1_M$ and which satisfies $\theta_{gh,x}=\theta_{g,hx}\theta_{h,x}$ as an equality of pulled-back module maps on $G\times_kG\times_kX$. These are sheaf-map identities and remain identities under arbitrary base change. Neither quasi-projectivity nor ampleness of $L$ is assumed. The scheme $X$ need not be connected or nonempty.

source.place: Supporting input, not asserted in Milne. WANTED: M. Brion, Algebraic group actions on normal varieties, arXiv:1703.09506v3, Lemma 2.9 (smooth case refers to Brion 2015, Theorem 2.14); finite disjoint-union extension supplied by the agent. The linearization and its cocycle are defined explicitly in the statement.

proof.text: The case $X=\varnothing$ has the unique isomorphism and identities, with $m=1$; hence assume $X\ne\varnothing$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian (its ring has just two ideals), [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $X$ locally Noetherian. For a quasi-compact open $V\subseteq X$, choose a finite affine open cover. Each coordinate ring is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], so each affine is a Noetherian space by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space], with finitely many irreducible components by [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components]. The closures in $V$ of these finitely many irreducible subsets cover $V$, so every maximal irreducible closed subset of $V$ is one of their maximal closures. Thus $V$ has finitely many components. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-locally-finite-components]: write $X$ as a disjoint open cover by normal integral schemes $X_i$. Each $X_i$ is clopen and therefore quasi-compact because $X$ is quasi-compact. Cover it by finitely many principal affine opens inside finite-type affine charts of $X$; adjoining the inverse of a principal-open equation preserves finite generation. Thus each $X_i$ is separated and finite type over $k$.

source.place: Tag 0357, lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles; local Noetherian hypotheses checked explicitly.

proof.text: The identity of $G$ is a $k$-point. By [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected], $G_K$ is connected for every field extension $K/k$, and remains connected after any further extension. Smooth maps are flat and locally finitely presented by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]; [lem-sfb-scheme-flat-smooth-point-base-change] therefore makes all projections $G\times_kT\to T$ smooth. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-connected-generic-geometry-core] first over $\operatorname{Spec}K$ and then over each $X_i$: its fibres are the geometrically connected $G_{\kappa(t)}$, and the identity section ensures nonemptiness. This proves that every $G_K$ and every $Y_i=G\times_kX_i$ is integral, and that $Y_i$ is normal. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] the projections $p_i:Y_i\to X_i$ and $Y_i\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ are finite type. Hence [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] gives local Noetherianity of $Y_i$. These products are separated: their diagonals impose the two factor-diagonal equations; on affine charts the corresponding defining surjections remain surjective after tensoring. Thus $G$ and $Y_i$ meet the integral separated finite-type hypotheses of Rosenlicht factorization.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, hypotheses for the product projection; geometry checked using the cited nodes.

proof.text: Choose $m\geq1$ from [lem-sfb-affine-group-picard-stable-exponent] and put $M=L^{\otimes m}$. On $Y_i$ set $D_i=(a|_{Y_i})^*L\otimes(p_i^*(L|_{X_i}))^\vee$ and $E_i=D_i^{\otimes m}$. Here the dual of a locally free rank-one sheaf is formed by the dual local frames, so evaluation identifies $D_i^{\otimes m}$ with $(a|_{Y_i})^*M\otimes(p_i^*(M|_{X_i}))^\vee$. Tensor pullback preserves those frames and their transition functions [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. If $\eta_i$ is the generic point of $X_i$ and $K_i=\kappa(\eta_i)$, the generic fibre of $p_i$ is $G_{K_i}$. The new Picard-exponent node applied to $D_i|_{G_{K_i}}$ gives $E_i|_{G_{K_i}}\cong\mathcal O_{G_{K_i}}$. This uses an arbitrary function field $K_i$, rather than assuming it algebraically closed.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, hypothesis (5); field-uniform torsion input is the new node (Brion Lemma 2.3 / Proposition 2.5).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-noetherian-generic-line-pullback] to $p_i:Y_i\to X_i$ and $E_i$. Both schemes are locally Noetherian; $X_i$ is normal integral; $p_i$ is smooth and therefore flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]; every fibre $G_{\kappa(x)}$ is nonempty integral by step 2; $p_i$ is finite type and the generic restriction is trivial by step 3. Obtain an invertible $B_i$ with $p_i^*B_i\cong E_i$. Pull back along $s_i:x\mapsto(e,x)$. Since $p_is_i=1$ and $as_i$ is the inclusion of $X_i$, the pullback composition identities [def-pc-module-pullback] give $B_i\cong s_i^*E_i\cong\mathcal O_{X_i}$. Consequently $E_i$ is trivial. Contracting its trivialization with the second line factor gives $\theta_i:p_i^*(M|_{X_i})\xrightarrow{\sim}(a|_{Y_i})^*M$. The disjoint open cover $\{Y_i\}$ of $G\times_kX$ glues these maps and their inverses to an isomorphism $\theta:p_2^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*M$. No assertion that the action preserves $X_i$ is needed here: $a|_{Y_i}$ has target $X$, and $M$ is defined on all of $X$.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, conclusion; identity-section restriction and disjoint-open gluing are written out.

proof.text: Along $s:x\mapsto(e,x)$, $s^*\theta$ is an automorphism of $M$. In a local frame this is multiplication by a unit $b$; changing the frame cancels the frame factor, so the local units glue to $b\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)^\times$. Replace $\theta$ by $\theta\circ p_2^*(b^{-1}\operatorname{id}_M)$. Its restriction to $s$ is now $b b^{-1}\operatorname{id}_M=\operatorname{id}_M$. This modification is a global sheaf isomorphism, not a choice on closed-point fibres.

source.place: Agent local-frame normalization, as in Brion (2015), Lemma 2.9 (primary publisher PDF read online; local copy WANTED).

proof.text: On $Z=G\times_kG\times_kX$, put $r(g,h,x)=(gh,x)$, $t(g,h,x)=(g,hx)$, and $v(g,h,x)=(h,x)$. The action identity identifies the targets of $A=r^*\theta$ and $B=(t^*\theta)\circ(v^*\theta)$; both map the pulled-back line $M_x$ to $M_{ghx}$. Thus $A^{-1}B$ is an automorphism of one invertible sheaf. The same local-frame calculation as in step 5 yields a global unit $u\in\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)^\times$. Restricting to $h=e$ gives $A=B=\theta_{g,x}$, and restricting to $g=e$ gives $A=B=\theta_{h,x}$, by the normalization and the unit action identity. Hence $u(g,e,x)=u(e,h,x)=1$ as equalities of regular functions on those subschemes.

source.place: Agent cocycle-defect calculation; compares the actual three pulled-back maps, as in Brion (2015), Lemma 2.9.

proof.text:
Fix $i$. A closed point exists on the nonempty finite-type $X_i$ by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], and is a $k$-point $x_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. Apply [lem-sfb-rosenlicht-product-unit-factorization] to the two nonempty integral separated finite-type schemes $G$ and $Y_i=G\times_kX_i$, the unit $u|_{G\times_kY_i}$, and the basepoints $e$ and $(e,x_i)$. Its regular-function identity yields
$$u(g,h,x)=u(g,e,x_i)\,u(e,h,x)\,u(e,e,x_i)^{-1}=1.$$
All three factors are $1$ by step 6. Therefore $u=1$ on the disjoint open cover of $Z$ by these products. It follows that $A=B$ globally, which is exactly the required cocycle identity for $\theta$.

source.place: Proposition 12.48, printed pp.246–247, formula (79); applied to G and G times one normal component.

proof.text: The normalized isomorphism for $M=L^{\otimes m}$ satisfies both required identities, so it is the asserted linearization. Applying any scheme base-change pullback functor preserves inverses, compositions and these equalities [def-pc-module-pullback]. Thus the identities remain identities after arbitrary base change, including nonreduced base changes; no pointwise-to-sheaf inference is involved. The construction used no ampleness, quasi-projectivity, or connectedness of $X$.
